newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end weaker, search for direction.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end weaker, search for direction.

text.p: Directionless Singapore shares closed weaker on Monday with dealers predicting a lacklustre week in the absense of any news to drive the market on.
"There's not a single sign of a new direction in the market," said one dealer with a local institution.
"There's no news in the market," another dealer said.
Inspiration could come from the U.S. if Wall Street maintains upward momentum, but dealers were otherwise looking for clues to determine what would move Singapore stocks.
The Straits Times Industrials Index dipped 4.58 to 2,060.90 at the close after spending much of the day virtually unchanged.
Market volume was a thin 116.1 million shares producing 209 losers against 134 gainers.
The most active share was over-the-counter traded Berjaya Industrial, which saw 10 million units change hands to see the stock end down Singapore $0.08 at S$1.62.
Foreign share tranches recovered through the day after slipping last week on proposals from Malaysia's Public Bank to relax rules on share buying by overseas investors.
Singapore Airlines foreign shares rose S$0.50 to S$12.70 on that upward wave combined with news that it was resuming link-up talks with Air India.
